headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write the runtime filesystem and use MCP; xonsh reads/writes the filesystem and executes shell/Python. If xonsh consumes OpenHands-produced files or logs as instructions, a shared mounted volume creates a realistic injection bridge. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted directory
IF xonsh parses OpenHands output files as commands or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic parsing of generated files
Add provenance tags to shared artifacts
Review any file-based handoff before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches mounted runtime files and handles model-provider API keys; xonsh reads filesystem contents, environment variables, and notebooks. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive files to the other, and OpenHands' broad network egress increases the chance of external transmission. This is a default-path concern if the same data directory is shared.
conditions: IF both agents share the same mounted workspace
IF sensitive files or environment variables are present in that workspace
mitigations: Use separate volumes for secrets and work files
Mount only least-privilege subdirectories
Redact secrets from shared notebooks and configs
Block outbound network for nonessential runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and shell execution, and OpenHands also modifies git state. On a shared directory, concurrent edits can clobber files or corrupt repository state; xonsh lacks multiple-instance support, so coordination is weaker. The overlap is directly documented for both agents, making write-conflict risk substantial.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF they run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Serialize access with a lock file
Assign disjoint output directories
Disable git writes for one agent
Run one agent at a time on shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code, shell actions, and browser-derived outputs; xonsh can execute shell commands and Python expressions. If xonsh treats OpenHands output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated text into executed commands or notebook actions. Because no verification step is documented between them, the pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes OpenHands output without human review
IF OpenHands output contains commands, code, or factual claims used downstream
mitigations: Require manual review before execution
Add schema validation for handoff files
Separate generation from execution roles
Log and diff all downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: OpenHands explicitly handles model-provider API keys and runs in a Docker runtime; xonsh is an isolated open-source shell environment with no requested secrets. The pair does not show a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch, but shared handling of mounted files can still create policy gaps if sensitive data is placed there. Only OpenHands is cited because the compliance-sensitive secret handling is specific to it.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF organizational policy forbids model-provider key material in the same runtime as user data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared mounts
Store API keys in separate secret stores
Document retention for runtime artifacts
Use distinct environments for regulated workloads
